newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil telecom law gets first rewrite.
newsitem.headline: Brazil telecom law gets first rewrite.

text.p: A first rewrite of a bill laying down the rules for privatization of Brazil's telecommunications industry was presented to a committee in the Chamber of Deputies with few alterations from its original text.
"The spine of the (government's) proposal has been kept although there are some different ideas," said Deputy Alberto Goldman, in charge of the bill in the lower house panel.
One new clause proposed by Goldman seeks to ensure immediate competition to privatized, regional blocks of federal telecommunications holding Telebras TELp._SA .
The article would oblige the government to publish simultaneously tender documents for the regional blocks and for a rival service in the same area.
"That would guarantee competition," Deputy Paulo Bornhausen, the president of the committee said.
Other changes to the bill include rules for new private operators on the installation of telephones in remote parts of Brazil and shorter terms for members of a new sector regulator.
Bornhausen said the committee would meet to discuss the changes April 8 and hoped the bill would be put to a vote in the panel in the week beginning April 21.
The government would then seek to put the bill to a vote on the floor of the Chamber of Deputies the following week.
Communications Minister Sergio Motta told reporters Wednesday he expected the bill would clear the Senate by the end of June.
